title: Saudi East-West pipeline — the outer bound of the officials' 3-5 week repair window closes
source: NEWS: Saudi Arabia shut the 1,200km East-West crude pipeline after drones hit it 'in the Riyadh and Medina areas' (aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/12/saudi-arabia-shuts-critical-oil-pipeline-after-drone-attack-what-happened, fetched direct 2026-09-15, HTTP 200), the Energy Ministry calling the shutdown a 'precaution' while 'specialised teams have begun steps to secure the pipeline and assess its safety'. Two officials speaking to the Associated Press put repairs at three to five weeks, relayed by Middle East Eye and investinglive (surfaced 2026-09-15). The DATE IS DERIVED, and that is the whole reason it is `estimate`: 2026-10-15 is five weeks from the shutdown, the outer bound of an officials' RANGE relayed through the press, not a milestone anyone has announced, and Riyadh has 'not yet disclosed the number of affected pumping stations or a restart timetable' (aljazeera.com 2026-09-14, fetched direct 2026-09-15). THE ANCHOR ITSELF IS DISPUTED BY ONE DAY: this calendar's opec-plus-meeting-2026-10-04 ledger and this event's own proposal date the attack 2026-09-10, while aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/12 and Reuters (via irishtimes.com, fetched direct 2026-09-15) both date it Friday 2026-09-11 — so the derived date carries a +-1 day error before the range's own four-week width is counted. Corroborating market read, machine-fetched DIRECT from the Polymarket gamma API (gamma-api.polymarket.com/events?slug=saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restarts-byptptpt) on 2026-09-15: restart-by 2026-09-15 at 0.65% ($62,856 traded), restart-by 2026-09-30 at 42% ($124,389), $187,246 total book, $61,636 liquidity, market end 2026-10-01T03:59Z, resolving on a Saudi government announcement that the pipeline 'is presently operating' (partial or reduced capacity qualifies; third-party attributions and future-tense statements do not). A web-search summary asserting the line was already 'pumping oil at its full capacity of 7 million barrels a day, according to a person familiar with the matter' on 2026-09-15 was DISCARDED as a date conflation: the 0.65% bid on the restart-by-09-15 leg refutes it directly, and the underlying headline is spglobal.com's 2026-03-10 story (slug 031026) about the March 2026 episode. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: CANONICAL ENTRY WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-15), promoting proposals/saudi-east-west-pipeline-repair-window-close-2026-10-15.from-jobs-2026-10-02.json, which now goes inert. The proposal's framing is affirmed and its two open questions are answered. WHY IT EXISTS, unchanged from the proposal: this calendar tracked NO entry of any kind for the outage that moved Brent from $97.92 (09-08) to $109.32 (09-15 live), and the only oil events in the corridor are OPEC's own meetings, which price policy rather than this supply break. WHAT THE DATE IS FOR, stated plainly so nobody reads more into it than it carries: it is the line past which a still-shut pipeline stops being a transient repair and starts being a structural supply premium. It is not a scheduled release, a vote, or an announcement, and no counterparty is obliged to do anything on it. TIER AFFIRMED medium, NOT raised: the physical event is large (4-5 mb/d, ~4-5% of global supply, the only route bypassing the blockaded Strait of Hormuz, on a line whose maximum capacity is 7 mb/d) but the DATE is an inference, symbols is [] and no house playbook covers commodities, so no date-keyed action is licensed at any tier. THE FINDING THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDS, and the reason the date is closer to the mode than the tail: the fast-restore precedents the press keeps citing are a milder severity class than this outage. April 2026 was a 700k bpd REDUCTION with the line still running, announced restored 2026-04-12 ('This quick recovery reflects the high operational resilience and crisis management efficiency of Saudi Aramco', Energy Ministry via aljazeera.com/economy/2026/4/12); March 2026 had Aramco's CEO promising full capacity 'in the next couple of days' (spglobal.com, 2026-03-10). Neither was a full precautionary shutdown of 4-5 mb/d with hits in two areas ~800km apart. The matching-severity analogue is 2019 Abqaiq, and it is the cautionary one: Aramco said on 2019-09-17 that it expected full capacity 'by the end of September' and full 12 mb/d capacity did not return until late November - an ~8-week slip in officials' own guidance in this exact setting. COUNTERWEIGHT, and why the base case is still an early partial restart: with Hormuz blockaded this line is Saudi Arabia's only export route, and Saudi buyers and traders told Reuters the Kingdom 'could begin to exhaust oil available for export within days unless it restores operations on the East-West pipeline' (via irishtimes.com 2026-09-15); Energy Aspects' Bronze 'expects that Saudi Arabia will be able to resume some flows through the pipeline while making repairs'. Partial capacity clears the announcement bar this event's own market resolves on. THE MEASUREMENT GAP WORTH KNOWING: the only traded instrument on the restart expires 2026-10-01, two weeks BEFORE this date, so there is no market-implied probability for a still-shut state on 2026-10-15 at all - the next pulse should check whether any October leg has opened. CORRIDOR: 32 tracked events sit within 5 days of this date and the two confirmed high-impact ones are cpi-2026-10-14 (the day before) and retail-sales-2026-10-15 (the same day), with iea-omr-2026-10-14 - the report that would actually quantify the supply loss - also the day before. Attribution on 10-15 is therefore already contested before the date arrives. Any lane that finds a Saudi government statement naming an actual restart or completion date should file THAT as its own entry; this row stays a derived threshold.
